chunks.explain: re is Python's module for regular expressions, which Rein uses to match command patterns.

hunks.where: at the top of the file

chunks.title: One import

chunks.explain: The whole policy is one function, decide(), and it checks things in a fixed order. Read-only tools are always allowed. Commands are checked against BLOCKED first, because deny rules beat allow rules. A command on the ALLOWED list runs without asking, but only if it has no chaining characters; otherwise python test_calc.py && curl evil.example would slip through, because it starts like an allowed command. Every other command asks you, and file edits ask you unless you chose --mode auto. Every Verdict carries a reason, and the model reads it, so it can change course.

hunks.diff:
+# ============ PERMISSIONS: allow, ask, or deny ============
+
+BLOCKED = [r"\brm\s", r"\bsudo\b", r"\bgit\s+push\b", r"\bcurl\b", r"\bwget\b"]  # never
+ALLOWED = [r"^python\s+test_\w+\.py\b", r"^python\s+-m\s+pytest\b"]            # always fine
+CHAINING = re.compile(r"[;&|`$<>]")  # an allowed command must not smuggle in a second one
+
+@dataclass
+class Verdict:
+    decision: str  # "allow", "ask", or "deny"
+    reason: str    # the model reads this too, so say why
+
+def decide(tool, args, mode):
+    """The policy. Deny rules are checked before allow rules."""
+    if tool.read_only:
+        return Verdict("allow", "read-only tool")
+    if tool.name == "run_command":
+        command = args.get("command", "").strip()
+        if any(re.search(p, command) for p in BLOCKED):
+            return Verdict("deny", "destructive, network, or admin command")
+        if any(re.search(p, command) for p in ALLOWED) and not CHAINING.search(command):
+            return Verdict("allow", "allow-listed command")
+        return Verdict("ask", "this command is not on the allow-list")
+    if mode == "auto":
+        return Verdict("allow", "edits are allowed in auto mode")
+    return Verdict("ask", "this tool changes files")
+
+def ask_human(call, reason):
+    answer = input(f"         ? allow {call.name}? ({reason}) [y/N] ")
+    return answer.strip().lower() == "y"
+
+
+
 # ============ THE LOOP ============

"""Create (or re-create) the small demo project that Rein practices on."""
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

demo = Path("demo")
shutil.rmtree(demo, ignore_errors=True)
demo.mkdir()

(demo / "calc.py").write_text("def add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n")

(demo / "test_calc.py").write_text("""from calc import add


def test_add():
    result = add(2, 3)
    assert result == 5, f"add(2, 3) returned {result}, expected 5"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_add()
        print("1 test passed")
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"test_add failed: {e}")
        raise SystemExit(1)
""")

(demo / "AGENTS.md").write_text("""# Rules for agents in this project
- Run the tests with: python test_calc.py
- Keep changes small. Do not rename functions.
- Never delete app.log. The support team reads it.
""")

lines = [f"2026-09-26 10:{i // 60:02d}:{i % 60:02d} INFO request {i} served in {5 + i % 7} ms"
         for i in range(1, 401)]
lines[396] = "2026-09-26 10:06:37 ERROR add(2, 3) returned -1, expected 5"
(demo / "app.log").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

# A second, empty project for the hostile tape: its one file is a link that points out of it.
import os
trap = Path("trap")
shutil.rmtree(trap, ignore_errors=True)
trap.mkdir()
(trap / "notes.txt").write_text("Nothing in this folder yet.\n")
os.symlink("../rein.py", trap / "link.txt")

print("Demo project ready: demo/calc.py, demo/test_calc.py, demo/app.log, demo/AGENTS.md")
